text:
sam-cust: Hey team — we're seeing intermittent high latency and doubled token billing for a long-polling endpoint. From our side traces show one request with X-Request-Id=rcpt-9a2f and the backend returning 200 then a sudden reconnect ~30s later. Billing shows two separate token charges for the same visible user action. Any idea? :confused:

eli-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the raw headers you captured? Is this using streaming (chunked) or the normal /v1/generate synchronous path?

sam-cust: It's our streaming client (we keep one connection per user, chunks of choices). Example headers we see on client: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED`, `X-Request-Id: rcpt-9a2f`, `X-Forwarded-For: 52.14.22.11`, `Connection: keep-alive`. We also have upstream proxy (company-proxy) in front. The reconnect looks like a client reconnect (we saw 100ms gap) but billing shows token usage both before and after.

eli-support: Got it. Two likely causes: 1) upstream or proxy is retrying or splicing the connection causing the runtime to see two separate requests with same user intent; 2) token accounting edge-case when a streaming session is torn down and retried. To investigate, can you run a minimal curl reproduction that keeps the connection open and prints raw bytes? That will let us see connection termination vs request reissue.

maria-eng: I'll add steps. Sam, please run from a machine behind the same proxy if possible. Replace <TOKEN> and <REQ> before sending. Run exactly:

```
curl -v --no-buffer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: <REQ>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --http1.1 \
  --raw \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream" \
  --output -
```

maria-eng: Important: use `--http1.1` (our streaming layer prefers it for keep-alive semantics), `--no-buffer` and `--raw` so curl doesn't hide chunk boundaries. Record the full stdout and stderr (`curl -v` gives headers). Also capture a full tcpdump if you can: `sudo tcpdump -i any port 443 -w ./stream.cap host api.redwood-inference.example` — attach both files.

sam-cust: Running now. Quick question: should I rotate token mid-connection to emulate our refresh? We do a silent refresh after 4m.

eli-support: Yes, if you can. After ~240s, run another request that exchanges the token and then attempt a graceful reconnect. Key things we need in the bundle: the curl stdout, curl stderr (with `-v`), `tcpdump` pcap, and your client logs showing the moment you saw a duplicate billing event and the exact local timestamp. Also include the exact value you used for `X-Request-Id`.

sam-cust: Attached logs: (pasting excerpt)
```
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood-inference.example\n> Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED\n> X-Request-Id: rcpt-9a2f\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n< Transfer-Encoding: chunked\n< content-type: text/event-stream\ndata: {"choices": [{"delta":"Hello"}], "usage": {"tokens": 12}}

# after 31.2s connection resets from proxy with RST
* Connection reset by peer
# client reconnects, sends identical X-Request-Id rcpt-9a2f
```

ops-oncall: :eyes: One more ask — enable trace headers by adding `X-Debug-Trace: on` to your reproduction so our infra can map the request across proxies and the runtime. Also include `--trace-ascii curl.trace` to get full timing.

maria-eng: Thanks. Once you upload the bundle, include these items in the support ticket: `trace_id` (if present), the `pcap`, `curl.trace`, `application log slice` (±2 minutes around the event), and the `support-bundle-id` you get from our upload tool. We'll run correlation across logs to see if the runtime accepted two separate sessions or if our billing pipeline double-counted a resumed stream.

sam-cust: Will do. Uploading now as sb-3091-7c4d. I also added `X-Debug-Trace: on` to the curl and rotated token after 4m — I see the same pattern, connection RST then reconnect with same X-Request-Id and two billing entries.

eli-support: Thanks — received sb-3091-7c4d. We'll correlate. For completeness, could you also run a short non-streaming reproduce (single POST to /v1/generate) with same token and X-Request-Id to prove it's specific to streaming semantics? Something like:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "X-Request-Id: rcpt-9a2f-sync" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"xlarge","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
```

maria-eng: One last note: if the proxy is doing a transparent retry on 502/timeout the client will likely not see it but the runtime will. We'll look for duplicate `ingress` logs with the same X-Request-Id but different connection IDs.

sam-cust: Copy — attaching the sync curl output too. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
